headline: Hackers gained access to OpenAI's internal monorepo via employee accounts
summary: A security research team chained two critical vulnerabilities, compromising OpenAI employee ChatGPT accounts and potentially accessing connected services like GitHub and Slack.
details: HacktronAI team compromised multiple OpenAI employee ChatGPT accounts on July 25, 2026, by chaining two critical vulnerabilities. This exploit granted them access to internal OpenAI repositories within 72 hours.
The compromised accounts could potentially access numerous connected services, including GitHub, Slack, and employee emails, due to how services were linked to ChatGPT and Codex.
To prove their access without learning sensitive information, the team used an employee's Codex to open a harmless pull request in OpenAI's internal monorepo, openai/openai.

The vulnerabilities included an SSO misconfiguration in OpenAI's identity infrastructure and a remote code execution (RCE) flaw in the libheif image-processing library used by OpenAI's Discourse community forum.
HacktronAI immediately reported the issues to OpenAI and Discourse, who quickly patched them. OpenAI awarded the team a $6,500 bounty for the OpenAI-side finding.

The libheif RCE vulnerability, dubbed "HEIF Heist," has wider implications, potentially affecting many applications that process user-controlled .heic/.heif/.avif images, including those used by Slack, Meta, and GitHub Enterprise.

headline_marked: [[Claude Code relaunches Projects]] for managing multiple AI agents in the cloud
headline: Claude Code relaunches Projects for managing multiple AI agents in the cloud
summary: The revamped Projects feature allows users to run multiple Claude Code agents with shared memory and goals. It's available in beta for select Pro and Max subscribers, with wider access coming soon.
details: Claude Code's revamped Projects feature allows users to control a team of AI agents that coordinate with each other. These agents operate under the same roof with shared memory, goals, and a library of files and artifacts, similar to other AI agent management tools.

Each project utilizes 'threads' for parallel tasks, directed by a 'coordinator.' Under the hood, each thread is a Claude Code cloud session working on its own branch, with merge conflicts resolved like standard pull requests.

Threads can further split work using subagents, loops, and workflows for faster completion. Users can interact with individual threads or monitor via the main project chat, with local tool support planned soon.

The updated Projects feature is currently in beta for select Claude Pro and Max subscribers. Access will expand to all Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users, as well as Cowork and regular Claude chats, later.
